components.name: Strip Cell

components.css: .ds-strip { border-top: 1px solid var(--color-tinta, #1a1a1a); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-tinta, #1a1a1a); background: var(--color-papel, #faf9f6); color: var(--color-tinta, #1a1a1a); font-family: var(--font-sans, "Public Sans", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-strip-cell { margin: 0; padding: 20px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; border-right: 1px solid var(--color-filete, #dfddd5); max-width: 260px; } .ds-strip-cell dt { font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-tinta-2, #595752); } .ds-strip-cell dd { margin: 0; } .ds-strip-fig { font-family: var(--font-serif, "Source Serif 4 Variable", ui-serif, Georgia, serif); font-size: 2.75rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-strip-note { font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.375; color: var(--color-tinta-2, #595752); } .ds-strip-note a { color: inherit; text-decoration: underline 1px var(--color-tinta-2, #595752); text-underline-offset: 3px; transition: text-decoration-color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-strip-note a:hover { text-decoration-color: var(--color-tinta, #1a1a1a); } .ds-strip-note a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-tinta, #1a1a1a); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Newsroom Instrument"**

A single page that reads like a data journalism piece and works like a measuring instrument. Warm paper, black ink, hairline rules and a serif for the numbers that matter. There are no cards, no shadows and no hero: the page is a grid of ruled cells and long columns, and the map of the six IPC regions sits at the top and drives everything under it.

Color is rationed. Ink does the talking, including the forecast. The Okabe-Ito palette exists only to tell regions apart and never carries text. Two grays carry meaning instead of decoration: a slate for energia (regulated tariff, shown as contrast) and a pale warm gray for estimates that cannot be told apart from zero. Uncertainty is always drawn, never implied.

Density is moderate and editorial: measured text columns (60 to 65ch), tabular figures everywhere, and charts that share one set of axes, fonts and halos so they read as one system.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and ink, flat, square corners (2px at most).
1px rules as the only structure: ink for major breaks, filete for minor ones.
Serif for headings and big figures, sans for interface, tables and axes.
Tabular numerals on every number, including selects and chart tips.
Region color for identity, ink for forecasts, gray for doubt.
Interaction is dry: 150ms ease-out, color and opacity only.

rules.name: The Ink Forecast Rule
rules.body: The forecast is ink, never region color. Dashed ink line (3 3), hollow end point, and a fan opening from the last real value: 80% band in ink at fill-opacity 0.22, 90% band in ink at 0.10. No forecast number appears without its band.

rules.name: The Fill-Only Rule
rules.body: Region colors are fills and strokes, never text. Amber and sky fail AA as text on paper, so every label, value and caption stays in ink or faded ink.

rules.name: The Energia Flag Rule
rules.body: Energia is always slate with the 4 3 dash. Bars get a slate fill at 0.35 opacity with a 1.25px dashed slate outline; lines and ranges are dashed slate strokes; points are solid slate. Wherever energia shows up in a chart, table or selector it carries the badge "Tarifa regulada - referencia de contraste" plus a one-line plain explanation.

rules.name: The Gray Means Zero Rule
rules.body: An estimate that cannot be told apart from zero is drawn in Doubt Gray, never in ink or region color, and the prose says so.

rules.name: The Tabular Everywhere Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on html and repeated on selects, chart SVGs and chart tips. Numbers line up in every column and never jitter when the region changes.

rules.name: The Serif Holds the Number Rule
rules.body: Big figures and headings are serif; axis labels, tables, selects in body size and controls are sans. Don't set a data table in serif or a headline figure in sans.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from 1px rules only. Ink rules mark section breaks, the strip, table heads and totals, and the underline of selects. Filete rules divide cells, rows and blocks. No boxes around content.

rules.name: The Map Governs Rule
rules.body: Choosing a region on the map, the GBA inset, the list under the map or the strip select updates the strip, the panel, the rubro view and the forecast section in the same render. One state, many readers.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. A state change is a background shift to Paper Shade, a weight change or an ink fill, never a shadow or a lift.

dos: Do set every number in tabular figures and every big number in Source Serif 4.
Do draw the forecast in ink with both bands (0.22 and 0.10) and print its 80% range next to the figure.
Do mark energia in slate with the 4 3 dash and the badge every time it appears.
Do gray out (no-significativo) any estimate whose range crosses zero, and say it in the text.
Do separate content with 1px rules: ink between sections, filete inside them.
Do keep transitions at 150ms ease-out on color and opacity only, and zero them under reduced motion.
Do label lines directly at their ends with a paper halo instead of using legends.
donts: Don't draw the forecast in a region color, least of all GBA blue.
Don't set text in region colors; amber and sky are fill only.
Don't use shadows, cards or radius above 2px.
Don't show a forecast or pass-through value without its range.
Don't use uppercase labels, eyebrows or kicker text above headings.
Don't draw any series that is not energia in slate; slate with the 4 3 dash means regulated tariff.
